newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo rubber prices fall, rain hits tapping.
newsitem.headline: Colombo rubber prices fall, rain hits tapping.

text.p: Rubber prices were slightly weaker at the Colombo auction on Thursday because of poor overseas demand but brokers and buyers said prices could rise if rain in tapping areas continues and reduces volume.
"Prices were slightly weaker because of poor offtake overseas," said a buyer. "But if rains continue and quantities are poor in the next two weeks then prices could go up."
Best latex crepe one-x, the purest grade, was unquoted as estates could not make good quality rubber because of rain. It went for 74 rupees ($1.30) per kg at Tuesday's auction. "The
market is not so hot as last year although prices for producers still remain excellent," said another buyer.
Brokers said heavy rain in tapping areas had reduced quality as well as volumes. They said 92 tonnes of crepe, 54 tonnes of scrap crepe and 20 tonnes of sheet were on offer.
Number one fell by two rupees to 70.50 rupees per kg with prices being in the 66-72 rupees per kg range. RSS1, unquoted on Tuesday, was 63.25 rupees. ($1=56.79 rupees)
